aërial: relating to the air; done in or through the air
aëronaut: a person who travels or navigates in a balloon
aloft: high up, above the deck or ground
ascensional: relating to rising upward, as a balloon does
astern: at or toward the back end of a ship
awning: canvas cover stretched over a deck or boat for shade
ballast: heavy material carried to adjust a balloon's height
biscuit: hard, dry bread kept as ship's food on long voyages
blow-pipe: narrow tube used to direct a jet of air into a flame
booty: goods or valuables seized from an enemy or in plunder
calorifere: device that heats air inside the balloon's envelope
carronades: short, heavy cannon once fitted on sailing ships
caravan: group of travellers journeying together, often across deserts
chests: large strong boxes used for storing goods
concave: curved inward, like the inside of a bowl
consul: official sent by a government to live and serve abroad
decomposition: breaking down of a substance into simpler parts
descry: catch sight of something faint or distant
dilate: expand or swell outward in size
equilibrium: state of balance, where opposing forces are equal
fatalist: person who believes all events are fixed and unavoidable
forecastle: raised front part of a ship's upper deck
gallons: units of liquid volume, about four litres each
glimpse: a brief, quick look at something
helicoidal: shaped like a spiral or coil
hermetically: sealed so tightly that air cannot get in or out
hydrogen: very light, flammable gas used to fill balloons
incredulous: unwilling or unable to believe something
indefatigable: tireless; unable to be worn out
intrepid: fearless and willing to face danger
ivory: hard creamy-white material from elephant tusks
latitude: distance north or south of the equator, measured in degrees
longitude: distance east or west of a starting meridian, measured in degrees
madman: a person who is insane or behaves recklessly
oscillations: regular swinging movements back and forth
pemmican: dried meat mixed with fat, a long-lasting travel food
platinum: heavy, precious silvery metal that resists corrosion
reconnoitre: survey an area ahead to gather information
replenish: refill something that has been used up
savage: uncivilised; a term once used for non-European peoples
sturgeon: large fish whose eggs are eaten as caviar
stopcock: valve that controls the flow of gas or liquid
sulphuric: relating to sulphur, especially a strong corrosive acid
trade-winds: steady winds blowing toward the equator over the oceans
valve: device that opens or closes to control flow through a pipe
vessel: ship or boat; also a container for liquid
